blocks.text: Naming is also a way of explaining

A name helps locate a piece of data and communicate what it represents. int bicicletas = 7; is more informative than int x2 = 7; if the quantity belongs to a rental. The compiler might accept either name; the difference lies in what a reader understands. For small problems, short, specific names reduce confusion between pieces of data.

We will choose names made of unaccented Latin letters, digits, and underscores, beginning with a letter: bicicletas, nivel2, paquetes_recibidos. This is a simple, safe convention for this course. C++ also allows other identifiers; we do not need every possibility to express these programs clearly.

An identifier cannot contain an internal space or a minus sign: paquetes nuevos and paquetes-nuevos are not valid single identifiers. It cannot begin with a digit either. Words such as int, return, and bool are reserved by the language and cannot be reused as variable names. Also avoid names beginning with an underscore and names used by the library, so you do not interfere with reserved or widely used identifiers.

options: It can only be used in file names.

blocks.explanation: int already names a language type, so it is not available as a name for a piece of data.

blocks.text: Capital letters are part of the name

cajas and Cajas are different names. If you define cajas and then try to read Cajas, the compiler cannot assume they mean the same thing. Using a consistent naming style helps you distinguish a typing mistake from two genuinely different pieces of data. It is also best not to create two variables differing only in capitalization if they describe different things: clearer names better explain their roles.

blocks.text: Choose names by purpose, not length

saldo_pendiente may be more useful than saldo if there is also a saldo_pagado. An overly long name makes code harder to read; an abbreviation without context forces readers to guess. Aim for a sufficient description. Do not choose names that promise something the code does not maintain: anterior must actually store the previous value, not merely bear that name.
